text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today to $457.22, continuing a sharp slide from its $478 high six days ago. The immediate pressure comes from the collapse in the U.S.–Brent crude spread: U.S. oil sits at $107.89 while Brent (the global benchmark) has spiked to $116, a six-month high on Middle East tensions and U.S.–Iran conflict escalation. For a refiner like Marathon, a wider gap between what crude costs globally versus domestically is a headwind—it cuts into the profit margin they make by turning cheap domestic oil into fuel. Refineries are running hard at 93.4% capacity, so they can't ease production to match tighter margins.

The broader issue is geopolitical: Middle East tensions and potential U.S. strikes on Iran are pushing global crude higher, but U.S. domestic supply remains plentiful (695 million barrels in storage). That leaves refiners squeezed between expensive global crude and a market flooded with cheap domestic feedstock, exactly the opposite of the tight-supply environment that usually benefits them.
